items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Nat Toles became the leader of that band and I stayed with that band.

ctx.x: Was your schooling at all interrupted by all that touring with the band?

Yeah, I did. You see, I finished. Then I didn't go to college until maybe after I'd been playing with Holder. You know, I didn't until I got a chance to -- I was playing with Holder. So when they said they'd give me a scholarship in music if I would come down and play with the band. So when I went -- that's when I went, like around 1930 -- after leaving Andy Kirk. See, I joined Andy Kirk and I went -- I says, "I think I'm going to take this up and go back home." So we went there and that's the band that Nat Toles…

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: No, I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band many times

ctx.x: No, I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band many times because Towl would leave sometimes and it wouldn’t be nobody but him. If we was supposed to leave at a certain time he would leave, and he left us, left me and Henry Coker, who later became a great trombone player man, and he left us in DesMoines, Iowa or somewhere. And we went out and picked pockets, somebody picked pockets, and we got our money back and more. I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-
